clue.text: Mollusc shell from Lima, just under half an inch across

indicators.note: a measurement taken across something spans it, so one piece stretches round the other

parts.note: a centimetre (CM) is about 0.39 of an inch, a little under half; its first letter opens the wrapper

indicators.note: the shell of a word is its outside, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of the Peruvian capital
the second letter of the centimetre abbreviation closes the wrapper

explanation.surface: A beachcomber picks up a tiny seashell in Peru, measuring not quite half an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation CM, a centimetre, is the length just under half an inch, and it goes round LA to make CLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a common bivalve, one specific kind of shellfish found burrowing in sand.

clue.text: Tory locum beginning to transmit disdain

parts.note: short for Conservative, the party of the Tories
a locum stands in temporarily, so is a temp

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of transmit

explanation.surface: A Conservative stand-in doctor starts broadcasting his scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name a feeling of scornful dismissal towards someone judged worthless.

clue.text: Drug sustaining a heavenly body!

parts.note: taken as written
a steroid is a drug, often a performance-enhancing one

explanation.surface: An excited claim that a drug keeps a gorgeous athlete going.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the drug sustains A by sitting beneath it, as a support would, so A is written first.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky object orbiting the sun, one kind of celestial object in space.

clue.text: Keeping birds, one caught cutting a bird of prey

indicators.note: something that cuts into a word goes inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a carrion-eating raptor
the Roman numeral for one
the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone keeping birds has one snapped up as a vulture slashes at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted pair goes in just after the bird's first letter, not at its middle, so the cut is near the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviculture is the formal term for the raising and care of birds, from the Latin avis.

clue.text: Sign right in middle of Spanish port

indicators.note: placing something in the middle of a word means it goes inside it

parts.note: Vigo is a port in Galicia, northwest Spain
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A signpost points right in the centre of a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is one of the twelve zodiac signs, the Virgin, astrologically linked to late summer births.

clue.text: Angry British editor of dubious pedigree

parts.note: cross means annoyed
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A furious British newspaper editor is sneered at for his mixed ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbred animal comes from parents of different breeds, so its lineage is mixed rather than pure.

clue.text: Insect collector left pet spider to one, unexpectedly

indicators.note: things arranged unexpectedly are not in the order you would predict

parts.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written
taken as written
Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A bug collector unexpectedly bequeaths their pet spider to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lepidopterist studies and collects butterflies and moths, the insect order Lepidoptera.

clue.text: On horseback, Ruth is arrogant

parts.note: a rider in the saddle is said to be up
ruth is an old word for compassion, surviving in ruthless

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth riding a horse looks down on everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like a name, but here it is the old noun for compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity describes someone self-important who behaves as though above their station.

clue.text: Uninhibited attention due to you once

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
thy is the archaic form of your, meaning belonging to you

explanation.surface: Someone free-spirited once got the attention they were owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour or talk is frank and coarse, unrestrained by polite squeamishness about bodily matters.

clue.text: Dark exclamation from protester?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not blond, of hair or complexion
second meaning: the cry of someone complaining of unjust treatment

explanation.walkthrough: Dark seems to describe a gloomy remark, but it is a definition in its own right, the opposite of fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means light-coloured, so dark hair is literally the negation; the phrase is also a protest against injustice.

clue.text: Poor Agnes beset by gold bits of furniture which took some cleaning

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: the name rearranged

indicators.note: something in poor shape is in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: tables are items of furniture

explanation.surface: Poor Agnes has a houseful of gilded tables that need endless polishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold and the furniture flank the jumbled name, one on each side, which is how it is beset.
explanation.definitionFit: Heracles' fifth labour was clearing King Augeas's stables, filthy from thirty years of uncleaned cattle dung.

clue.text: How many people solve the Times cryptic, theoretically?

definitions.text: How many people solve the Times cryptic
definitions.meaning: first meaning: printed out in the newspaper, with a pen, rather than on screen
second meaning: in principle, though perhaps not in practice

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as a question about numbers of solvers; it really asks in what manner they solve.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in plans or calculations but may fail in reality.

clue.text: Say, Ron's brother's admitting evidence of debt? That's appalling!

parts.note: e.g. means for example, used just as say is

indicators.note: admitting something means letting it in, so it is placed inside

parts.note: Ron and Reg Kray were notorious London gangster twins; Reg's gives REGS
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of money owed

explanation.surface: Shock that a gangster's brother has signed for debts.
explanation.walkthrough: Ron suggests Ron Weasley, but the Krays were twin East End gangsters of the 1960s, Ronnie and Reggie.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means outstandingly bad or shocking, as an egregious error is a glaring one.

clue.text: Get rid of Democrat before long

parts.note: standard abbreviation
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: An instruction to dump the Democrat soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before long' reads as a phrase meaning soon, but before is just placing D ahead and long is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is informally to discard or abandon it.

clue.text: North happily distributed charity

indicators.note: things distributed are spread out and scattered, losing their original order

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: Donations were cheerfully handed out across the north of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Philanthropy is generous giving to good causes, the love of humankind shown in donations.

clue.text: Most vulgar traits we'd worked on

indicators.note: material worked on is reshaped, so these letters are remodelled

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone has been cultivating the coarsest of personal characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry means cheap and showy, so the superlative describes the gaudiest, most tasteless thing.

clue.text: Romantic that is embracing old ringmaster

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap the arms around, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.
Muhammad Ali, the late boxing champion, was master of the ring

explanation.surface: A sentimental type hugs a retired circus ringmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A ringmaster belongs in a circus, but here the ring is a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun a romantic is a dreamer who sees the world through hopeful, unrealistic eyes.

clue.text: An exclamation on seeing how Eliot's poems were signed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old-fashioned cry of surprise
second meaning: the novelist Mary Ann Evans wrote as George Eliot, so her work was credited to that pen name

explanation.walkthrough: Eliot suggests T. S. Eliot the poet; it is George Eliot, the Victorian novelist who also published poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild oath of astonishment, and also literally the authorship credit on George Eliot's verse.

clue.text: Fast start from a quiet side of Yorkshire

parts.note: taken as written
the call for silence
Sheffield Wednesday is a Yorkshire football team, and a team is a side

explanation.surface: A speedy beginning from a peaceful corner of northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast start sounds like a quick getaway, but fast is the noun for going without food. Sheffield Wednesday is a professional football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy day opens Lent, the forty-day Christian season of fasting before Easter.

clue.text: Head of Supreme Court about to shred legal document

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Supreme

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: standard abbreviation
to rip is to tear apart

explanation.surface: The chief justice is poised to tear up a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Supreme Court' reads as a chief justice, but only the first word is beheaded; Court stays whole as CT.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a script is the original or principal written instrument, as opposed to a copy.

clue.text: Parasite found in contents of Samos kebab

indicators.note: the contents of a word are what lies within its outer shell, so only the inside letters count

parts.note: Samos without its first and last letters
kebab without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A health scare: a bug lurking inside a kebab bought on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a hidden word running across the two, but it is each word's insides joined. Samos is a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Some amoebae, like the one causing dysentery, live off a host organism, so the single-celled creature counts.

clue.text: Minute break lying back in hammock

indicators.note: lying back suggests running backwards, so the letters are read right to left
the letters sit inside the following word

parts.note: the inner letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone takes a short rest, reclining in a hammock.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute break suggests a brief nap, which fits the hammock scene; read minute as tiny, a little pause in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma is the punctuation mark for a slight pause, a tiny interruption inside a sentence.

clue.text: Reproduce shocking article about European power

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged word wraps the rest
something shocking is disturbing, and disturbed letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A scandalous newspaper piece about European might is copied everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The word article is itself the fodder, not a hint for A or THE, and the European power sits near the front of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To replicate is to make an exact copy, duplicating something as cells or experiments do.

clue.text: A silver-lined handheld comms device

indicators.note: a lined garment has material along its inside, so one piece sits within

parts.note: per means for each, as a does in 'ten pounds a head'
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A gadget for messaging with a silver interior.
explanation.walkthrough: A looks like the article to take as written; it means per, as in miles an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager, or bleeper, is a small portable receiver that beeps to alert someone to a message.

clue.text: Kill enemy guarding large object at sea

parts.note: ice is slang for murder

indicators.note: a guard stands round what it protects, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
standard clothing-size abbreviation

explanation.surface: Orders to kill the enemy who is protecting a big thing out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice floe is a flat sheet of floating ice, something drifting in the water of polar seas.

clue.text: Good German downhiller having shed kilo is more feisty

parts.note: gut is the German word for good

indicators.note: having shed something means having dropped it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a skier goes downhill
K is kilo in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A fine German ski racer has lost weight and is feeling plucky.
explanation.walkthrough: Good German suggests a person, but it is the German word for good. Removing K from SKIER leaves SIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutsy means brave and spirited, so its comparative describes someone with more pluck.

clue.text: Turncoat Yankee hosting Poles for a short time

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: a turncoat changes sides, betraying them
Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet
north and south, the two poles

explanation.surface: An American defector briefly takes in some Polish visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like people from Poland; it is the two magnetic poles, north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: Transitory things are fleeting and impermanent, lasting only briefly before passing.

clue.text: Beastly house by end of esplanade that's an eyesore

parts.note: a sty is a pigs' home, a house for beasts

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: last letter of esplanade

explanation.surface: An ugly building at the end of the seafront spoils the view.
explanation.walkthrough: Eyesore reads as an ugly sight; taken literally it is a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a painful spot on the eye.
